newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says more rice imports unlikely in 96.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says more rice imports unlikely in 96.

text.p: The Philippines is unlikely to need further rice imports for the rest of this year because of prospects of improved harvests and ample reserves, an agriculture official said on Monday.
The official, who declined to be named, said the Philippines has a buffer stock of 1.4 million tonnes of the staple food of the country's 68 million people.
"The country's national rice inventory from commercial, household and government warehouses is still good for 70 days," the official added.
President Fidel Ramos ordered the Department of Agriculture to ensure it maintains a 90-day inventory totalling 1.8 million tonnes in the period from July 1 to September 30, a seasonally lean period.
Ramos's order followed a rice shortage last year which sent prices soaring and caused a sharp rise in inflation.
Philippine officials have said the total area planted to rice has increased this year, partly as a result of a government credit programme to encourage output.
The Philippines has imported 846,000 tonnes since the start of the year. - Manila newsroom 63 2 8418938 Fax 8176267
